StockAdjustmentItemSerializer.validate_p.justification: `backup_value=False` of `get_global_setting`: it only applies when the setting is not defined, which cannot happen for `STOCK_ALLOW_OUT_OF_STOCK_TRANSFER` (declared with a default); and the `cache` argument cannot be distinguished in the unit-test configuration (the test `test_validate_pk_does_not_use_a_cached_setting_value` exists but passes with either value because the test settings do not enable the settings cache). The `cache=False` argument of `StockItem.delete` IS observable and is killed (`test_delete_does_not_use_a_cached_setting_value`).

StockAdjustmentSerializer.validate|delet.justification: The base `serializers.Serializer.validate` returns its argument unchanged and its return value is discarded: deleting the call has no effect.

StockAddSerializer.save|or -> and| or.justification: Redundant guard: for quantity 0 (or negative) `add_stock` itself returns False (model-level guard), so skipping the item in `save()` is unobservable.

StockAddSerializer.save|POSITIVE_GUARD q.justification: Redundant guard (see above): the model-level `quantity <= 0` check returns False anyway.

StockRemoveSerializer.save|or -> and| or.justification: Redundant guard: for quantity 0 `take_stock` itself returns False, so the serializer-level skip is unobservable.

StockItem.take_stock|POSITIVE_GUARD quan.justification: First `quantity <= 0` guard: the second guard after the `min()` clamp rejects the same input, so moving this boundary has no effect.

StockAdjustView.get_serializer_context|d.justification: DRF `GenericAPIView.get_serializer_context` already supplies `request`; the explicit assignment is redundant.

StockItem.updateQuantity|False -> True|F.justification: `save(add_note=False)` -> `add_note=True`: the flag only controls the 'created' audit note and is ignored for an existing row (`if self.pk`), and updateQuantity only saves existing items.
